Landing.honestText: You get an approximate estimate of your level by IELTS criteria — a broad range, not an exact band and not an official result. GoNative Exams is not connected with IELTS or its owners. We test the feedback on our own sets of essays with known mistakes before every change; the real value is in the comments: what to fix and why.
Landing.guideText: Our free guide covers the test format, how scores work and how to prepare, with the most detail on Writing.

freeItems.feedbacks: 2 full feedbacks a month — two tasks or one full test
freeItems.practice: Practice on your weak points and word lists

official.q: Is this my official IELTS result?
official.a: No. The ranges are approximate practice estimates. Only an official IELTS test gives you an official result.

accuracy.a: Yes. Feedback is produced automatically with AI and can miss a mistake or mark correct language. We measure it on our own essay sets before every change and keep checking it; you can report any comment you disagree with.

training.q: Is my writing used to train AI?
training.a: No. Your text is sent to our AI provider only to produce your feedback and is not used to train models.

price.a: You can start for free: 2 feedbacks a month, unlimited drafts.

languages.q: In which languages are the explanations?
languages.a: In English, Russian or Ukrainian — you choose. The site itself is in the same three languages.

variants.a: Both. Academic Task 1 reports and General Training letters each have their own tasks and feedback; Task 2 and the full test work for both.

computer.q: Why type instead of writing by hand?
computer.a: IELTS is now taken on computer, so typing an essay against the clock is part of the skill. Our editor counts your words and the timer works like the real one.

tasks.q: Can I check an essay on my own task?
tasks.a: Yes, for Task 2: paste your own question. Task 1 reports and letters use our tasks, because the feedback needs the chart's data or the letter's situation to check your answer.

ielts-writing-task-2-checker.title: IELTS Writing Task 2 checker
ielts-writing-task-2-checker.lead: Write an essay on one of our tasks or your own question and get feedback on each of the four criteria, with every comment tied to the words it is about.

checks.response: Whether you answer the exact question, keep a clear position where one is asked for and develop your ideas.
checks.coherence: How your paragraphs progress, whether linking words fit the logic and references are clear.
checks.lexical: Precision of words and collocations, word forms, spelling and repetition.
checks.grammar: The range of your sentence structures and the mistakes that repeat across the essay.

own.q: Can I check an essay on my own question?
own.a: Yes. Paste your own Task 2 question, or choose one of our tasks.

score.q: Do I get a band score?
score.a: You get an approximate range for each criterion, not an exact band or an official result. The comments matter more than the numbers.

time.a: About half a minute after you submit. You can write with a 40-minute timer, as in the test.

ielts-academic-task-1-checker.metaTitle: IELTS Academic Writing Task 1 checker: feedback on charts and graphs · GoNative Exams
ielts-academic-task-1-checker.metaDescription: Describe a line graph, bar chart, pie chart or table and get feedback on your overview, key features and figures — checked against the chart's data. Free to try.
ielts-academic-task-1-checker.title: IELTS Academic Task 1 checker
ielts-academic-task-1-checker.lead: Describe one of our charts and get feedback that knows the data: whether your overview sums up the main trends, which key features you chose and whether your figures and comparisons are right.

checks.overview: Whether a clear overview sums up the main trends in one place.
checks.features: Whether you chose the key features and supported them with figures.
checks.figures: Every figure is checked against the chart's data; comparisons like "twice as many" must be true.
checks.language: The language of trends and comparisons, word forms and grammar.

own.q: Can I upload my own chart?
own.a: Not yet: the feedback needs the chart's data to check your figures, so you write on our charts. They cover line and bar charts, pie charts, tables and combinations.

score.q: Do I get a band score?
score.a: You get an approximate range for each criterion, not an exact band or an official result.

time.q: How long should my report be?
time.a: At least 150 words in about 20 minutes; the editor counts your words and has an optional timer.

ielts-general-training-letter-checker.metaTitle: IELTS General Training letter checker: Task 1 feedback · GoNative Exams
ielts-general-training-letter-checker.metaDescription: Write an IELTS General Training Task 1 letter — formal, semi-formal or personal — and get feedback on tone, the three bullet points and your language. Free to try.
ielts-general-training-letter-checker.title: IELTS General Training letter checker
ielts-general-training-letter-checker.lead: Write a formal, semi-formal or personal letter for one of our situations and get feedback on what matters most in Task 1: the tone for the reader, all three points and the language.

checks.points: Whether each of the three bullet points is covered and developed.
checks.tone: Whether the tone suits the reader, from the greeting to the sign-off.
checks.organisation: Paragraphs, the opening line and how the letter moves from point to point.
checks.language: Vocabulary and grammar, with personal-letter style treated as natural where it fits.

own.q: Can I check a letter on my own situation?
own.a: Letters are written on our situations: the feedback needs the reader, tone and three points of the task to check them.

score.q: Do I get a band score?
score.a: You get an approximate range for each criterion, not an exact band or an official result.

tone.q: Are contractions allowed in a letter?
tone.a: In a letter to a friend, yes — contractions, phrasal verbs and everyday phrases are natural. In a formal letter, keep a polite, neutral style.

Reading.factFormat: A full test has three passages and 40 questions in 60 minutes; one passage takes about 20 minutes.
Reading.factMarking: Answers are checked against the key straight away — spelling counts, as in the exam.

Listening.title: IELTS Listening
Listening.lead: Practise Listening in the format of the computer-delivered test: four recordings, 40 questions and an instant, detailed review with the transcript.
Listening.factFormat: A full test has four parts and 40 questions, about 25 minutes of recordings; one part takes about 6 minutes.
Listening.factModes: In exam mode you hear each recording once, without pausing. In practice mode you can pause, go back and slow down.
Listening.factBand: After a full test in exam mode you also see an approximate band from the official score thresholds.
